BHARATHIAR UNIVERSITY
Bharathiar University, established in Coimbatore in 1982 under the Bharathiar University Act, 1981(Act I
of 1982) originated from the former Postgraduate Centre of the University of Madras. Recognized by the UGC in
1985, the University today comprises 39 departments offering 54 postgraduate programmes, along with M.Phil.
and Ph.D. degrees. With jurisdiction over Coimbatore, Erode, Tirupur and The Nilgiris, it affiliates 145 colleges.
The University holds an ‘A++’ grade in the NAAC Fourth Cycle and ranks 10th among State Public Universities in
NIRF 2025, 46th under the University category, and 76th overall. Internationally, it is placed in the 601–800 band
of the ‘The World University Rankings 2026’ and 201–250 among Young Universities. Bharathiar University
fosters advanced research, industry-integrated curricula, strong digital and library resources, and supports
innovation through its IPR Cell and DRDO-BU Life Sciences Centre. Its Centre for International Affairs facilitates
global academic collaboration and international student admissions.
Bharathiar University is located in Coimbatore, Tamil Nadu, a vibrant educational and industrial hub
popularly known as the "Manchester of South India" due to its prominent textile industry. The University campus
is situated amidst the scenic foothills of the majestic Western Ghats, a UNESCO-recognized biodiversity hotspot,
providing a serene and conducive environment for academic pursuits and research.
Nestled at the foothills of the renowned ‘Maruthamalai Murugan Temple’, one of the most revered
hill temples dedicated to Lord Murugan, the University enjoys a unique blend of natural beauty, cultural
heritage and spiritual significance. The campus is also located in close proximity to the internationally
acclaimed philosophical Isha Yoga Center.
The region surrounding the University is characterized by rich biodiversity, pleasant climatic conditions
and panoramic views of the Western Ghats. Coimbatore's strategic location, excellent connectivity by road, rail
and air, and its growing reputation as a centre for education, innovation and entrepreneurship make Bharathiar
University an ideal destination for higher learning and academic excellence.
ABOUT THE DEPARTMENT
The Department of Linguistics, established in
1985, has been actively engaged in advanced
research and teaching, offering M.A. and
Ph.D. programmes in Linguistics. Alongside its
academic work, the department undertakes
socially relevant extension activities in areas
such as tribal literacy, adult literacy, and
teacher training. Its M.A. Linguistics programme is innovative, combining core and applied linguistics
with unique interdisciplinary supportive papers that attract students from science backgrounds.
GLIMPSE OF DEPARTMENT’S ACADEMIC JOURNEY ACROSS 4 DECADES
The department reached several significant milestones in its academic journey. It successfully
completed two phases of the UGC-SAP-DRS programme, focusing on the language and culture of
indigenous communities of the Western Ghats, and received the prestigious Endangered Languages
Scheme from the UGC. A collaboration with the University of Malaya, an outbound program for
Malaysian students to undergo linguistics training availing the service of its faculty and eminent Indian
linguists. It has been conducting academic events regularly, including National, International
Conferences and Workshops, Orientation Programmes, using the service of Internationally Trained
Faculty. Member’s This iconic department continues to be a vibrant Centre for linguistic scholarship.
Knowledge dissemination
To date, The department has published 55 books and 3 monographs, produced 139 Ph.D. and
50 M.Phil. scholars, and annually publishes an International peer reviewed Journal in the name of
'Working Papers in Linguistics and Literature’ (UGC-CARE listed for 3 years) and Students’ Newsletter
‘Voice of Linguistic Novices’. It hosts the ‘Telugu Chair’ for research on Telugu-speaking minorities in
the Coimbatore region. The department completed around 30 major /minor research projects funded
by UGC, RUSA, ICSSR, CIIL, and others. It has been organizing weekly Research Circle Meeting, called
Saussure's Knowledge Factory for budding linguists. It has conducted over 100 international and
national seminars, conferences, and workshops.
LINGUISTIC SOCIETY OF INDIA (LSI)
The Linguistic Society of India is a body of intellectuals working on languages and
promotion of Linguistics. The Society has been in existence since 1928 and built a strong network of
Linguistics scholars. Over the years, LSI has also become a household name among the linguists of
this country. The society organises an annual conference attracting a wide range of participation from
India and abroad. These events bring together generations of linguists. So far, the society has
organised 47 events, and the 48th one is being organized this year.

SUBMISSION OF ABSTRACTS
The Department of Linguistics, Bharathiar University, Coimbatore, is delighted to
announce the 48th International Conference of the Linguistic Society of India (ICOLSI-48), to be
held from 18th to 20th November 2026. ICOLSI is the flagship conference of the Linguistic
Society of India and is held annually. We welcome submissions of original research from
scholars, researchers and students for presentation and scholarly discussion at this
distinguished conference.
This conference adopts the theme “Exploring the Unearthed System of Systems in
Linguistics” to encourage a deeper understanding of language as a complex network of
interconnected systems. Linguistics traditionally examines various subsystems such as
phonetics, phonology, morphology, syntax, semantics, pragmatics, discourse, and
sociolinguistics. However, these components do not function in isolation; rather, they interact
dynamically to form a broader system of language. The theme invites scholars to uncover and
examine these often-overlooked interrelationships, revealing how linguistic structures,
cognitive processes, social contexts, cultural practices, and technological developments
collectively shape human communication. By exploring language as a “system of systems,” the
conference aims to foster interdisciplinary dialogue, innovative theoretical perspectives, and
new methodologies that contribute to a more comprehensive understanding of language, its
evolution, and its role in society.
CONFERENCE THEME:
EXPLORING THE UNEARTHED SYSTEM OF SYSTEMS IN LINGUISTICS
NON-THEMATIC SESSIONS
In addition to the thematic sessions, the conference will also include non-thematic
sessions covering a wide range of topics in linguistics. These sessions are open to all areas of
linguistic research, including but not limited to phonetics, phonology, morphology, syntax,
semantics, pragmatics, sociolinguistics, psycholinguistics, computational linguistics,
historical linguistics, and allied areas of linguistics. We encourage submissions that present
innovative research, theoretical insights, and empirical findings across the diverse spectrum
of linguistic inquiry. These sessions aim to provide a platform for scholars to share their work
and engage in discussions spanning the breadth of linguistic studies.
ABSTRACT SUBMISSION GUIDELINES
Abstract submissions must be anonymised and uploaded through ‘EasyAbs’
(https://easyabs.linguistlist.org/conference/ICOLSI-48/). This practice promotes a fair,
transparent and constructive assessment process by enabling reviewers to evaluate
submissions solely on their academic merit. Abstract for oral presentations on any original
and unpublished research on all aspects of theoretical, applied and interdisciplinary
linguistics. Scholars and academicians are encouraged to submit abstracts of their papers in
about 250-300 words in any of the related areas in PDF/Docx format. To ensure fairness for
all participants, the conference will permit only one first-author submission per participant.
For every paper accepted for oral, at least one author must complete an individual
conference registration.

Concept Note
The conference, to be held on the theme of “Exploring the Unearthed
System of Systems in Linguistics”, seeks to advance a holistic
understanding of language as a complex and dynamic network of
interconnected systems. The diverse domains of linguistics - including
phonetics, phonology, morphology, lexicology, syntax, discourse
analysis, pragmatics, semantics, applied linguistics, sociolinguistics, and
related fields - do not operate in isolation; rather, they interact and
converge to constitute the broader architecture of human language.
Exploring these nuances and intricate interconnections among them
offers valuable insights into how linguistic structures, cognitive
processes, social contexts, cultural practices, and technological
advancements collectively shape human communication. It is known
fact that viewing language as a “system of systems” with the lenses of
other disciplines encourages scholars to move beyond conventional
disciplinary boundaries and explore emerging relationships among
linguistic phenomena. Such an approach has the potential to generate
innovative theoretical perspectives, interdisciplinary methodologies,
and new directions for understanding the structure, evolution,
diversity, and societal role of language and it's various manifestations.
Thus, the present conference aims to provide an inclusive and
intellectually stimulating platform for scholars, researchers, and
students to present innovative research, theoretical insights, and
empirical findings across the full spectrum of linguistic inquiry. By
fostering meaningful academic dialogue, interdisciplinary
collaboration, and the exchange of diverse perspectives, the
conference aspires to open up new dimensions of linguistic research
and contributes to shaping future directions in the field of Linguistics.

Tourist Attractions Around Coimbatore
Maruthamalai
Maruthamalai Murugan Temple is known for its high
vibrations and revitalizing atmosphere. The Dravidian-
architecture of the temple is completely awe-inspiring.
Isha Yoga Centre
The Isha yoga center situated at the foothills of Velliangiri
on the outskirts of Coimbatore, is the headquarters for
Isha yoga.
Kovai Kutralam
It is a scenic spot with a gentle waterfall originating on
the Siruvani hill ranges. Waterfalls around the forests
ranges is the beauty of this place.
Anaikatti
One of the most picturesque places in India's south is
Anaikatti, Coimbatore. With its picturesque waterfalls and
surrounding lush greenery. It is located directly where
Tamil Nadu and Kerala state borders meet.
Gedee Car Museum
One of the top places to visit for car and bike lovers
which is an amalgamation of vintage and new cars that
are transported to the Museum all the way from
countries like US, UK, Japan and Germany.
Perur Patteeswarar Temple
It is quite an ancient temple which was built to worship
Lord Pateeswara Swamy (Lord Shiva). It is largely known
for its grand architecture, ancient artwork, paintings,
sculptures, carvings, and relics.
Ooty
It is a beautiful hill town which is famous for natural
beauty, tranquility and uniqueness. It is called as the
Queen of hill stations and is an important tourist
attraction.
Coonoor
Coonoor is a hill station in the southern Indian state of
Tamil Nadu. It’s known for its tea estates in the
surrounding Nilgiri hills. Sim’s Park is a sprawling public
garden with plants like rhododendrons, roses and
eucalyptus trees.

Venue
The Dr. USHA KIRTILAL MEHTA CONVENTION CENTRE, located within the picturesque campus of
Bharathiar University, Maruthamalai Road, Coimbatore, serves as an ideal venue for academic and
professional gatherings. Nestled at the foothills of the Maruthamalai Hills, part of the renowned Western
Ghats, the convention centre offers a serene and inspiring environment. The facility features a spacious
auditorium with a seating capacity of over 1,000 participants, along with ample parking facilities. The
exhibition area, seminar halls, and food court are conveniently situated near the main auditorium, ensuring
ease of access and comfort for delegates. The venue is well connected to major transportation hubs, being
approximately 20 km from Coimbatore International Airport (CJB), 10 km from Coimbatore Railway Station
(CBE), and 10 km from the Central Bus Stand (Gandhipuram), making it easily accessible for both national
and international participants.
